title: Viewport resilience & density-aware interaction tuning for Console surfaces
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Improve the Redwood Console's surface stability across a wide range of viewport sizes, device pixel densities, and browsers. This ticket covers density-aware layout rules, touch/gesture interaction refinements, and cross-browser fallbacks for tables, charts (canvas/SVG), and stacked modals. Deliverables: Figma prototypes for compact/dense and expanded states; a small interaction spec for scroll locking and modal stacking; a cross-browser QA checklist; and a set of design decisions for engineering implementation (CSS, layout math, and animation budgets).

Background: Recent QA and customer reports surfaced subtle breakage when dashboards are used on narrow viewports (small laptops, large tablets) and on high-DPI displays. Issues include: table column truncation with inconsistent ellipsis behavior across Safari/Firefox, chart canvas pixelation and rerender jank during resize, modal backdrop blur causing performance regressions on older macOS, and keyboard focus lost when modals are stacked or when virtualized tables rerender rows. Engineering has pushed a few fixes (virtualization tweaks, pointer-event adjustments), but we need definitive design guidance to ensure consistent UX and to avoid repeated regressions.

Constraints and trade-offs: We must balance compact density (allowing more rows/panels visible for power users) against legibility and discoverability for occasional users. Some visual effects (backdrop blur, heavy box-shadows) are expensive on certain GPUs — provide viable fallbacks. Prefer CSS-first solutions (container queries, clamp(), subgrid where available) but document polyfills/fallbacks and when JS measurement is acceptable. Keep animation budgets small to preserve 60fps on mid-range devices and avoid layout-thrashing during autosizing.

Approach: 1) Define three density tiers (cozy, compact, dense) with explicit spacing tokens and font scaling; 2) Create container-query-driven layout rules for dashboard panels so charts and tables reflow predictably; 3) Standardize table cell truncation and tooltip fallbacks for overflowing content; 4) Create a modal stacking model: z-index map, focus-trap rules, backdrop fallbacks (blur vs. semi-opaque color), and scroll-lock strategy that works across Chrome/Safari/Firefox and iOS; 5) Chart guidance: use devicePixelRatio-aware canvas resizing, debounce layout changes, and provide a low-cost placeholder strategy while rerendering; 6) Prototypes and QA scenarios to capture regressions and performance metrics.

Deliverables: - Figma file with density tokens, example dashboards, table states, stacked modal flows, and responsive breakpoints. - Interaction spec (MD) with focus behavior, keyboard nav, and touch gestures. - Cross-browser QA checklist and known-bug matrix. - Hand-off notes for engineering with explicit CSS rules, performance caveats, and aria/a11y expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Design prototypes exist for three density tiers (cozy/compact/dense) covering dashboard, cost view, rollout list, and modal flows in the Figma Console-UX file.
Interaction spec documents modal stacking behavior (z-index map, focus trap, backdrop fallback) and scroll-lock strategy with at least two implementation patterns (CSS-only + JS fallback).
Table cell overflow behavior defined: consistent ellipsis, accessible tooltip on hover/focus, and mobile wrap/stack pattern for narrow viewports.
Chart resizing guidance documented: devicePixelRatio-aware canvas resizing example, debounce strategy, and placeholder while re-rendering.
Cross-browser QA checklist created with reproducible steps for Chrome, Firefox, Safari (desktop and iOS), and Edge including performance expectations.
Design sign-off from PM (Ava Thompson) and Engineering lead (Diego Ramos) recorded in comments.
Prototype tested on target devices and a short summary of observed perf (fps) and layout regressions attached to the ticket.

2026-02-25 Nina Hart (PM): Reviewed prototypes; asked for clearer keyboard nav examples for stacked modals and confirmation that aria-modal will be preserved for nested dialogs.
2026-03-02 Maya Patel: Added compact-density variants for the rollout list with new spacing tokens and example of table row density switcher (visual + persisted setting).

2026-03-05 Diego Ramos (Eng): Implemented a small demo PR that applies container queries to dashboard panels and shared perf numbers — observed ~10-15% CPU decrease on mid-range laptops when debouncing chart resize. PR: github.com/redwood/console/pull/4578

2026-03-08 Accessibility review by Noor Singh: flagged focus loss on stacked modals when backdrop uses pointer-events: none — suggested explicit focus-trap in JS and clearer visible focus indicators for compact density.
